title: Release audit: README.md still documents `.../v0.1.0/install.sh` for the install command and fo
summary: Update both documented commands to the current release installer (v0.1.1 or a versionless latest URL) and add a README guard test that asserts the install and uninstall commands use the release installer.
requirements: R1: README.md contains no reference to the `v0.1.0` install script URL (`.../v0.1.0/install.sh`), in the install command or anywhere else.
R2: The README install command and the README uninstall command reference exactly the same install-script URL, and that URL is the only install-script URL in README.md.

R3: The install-script URL in README.md points at the release whose behavior the documentation describes (the current release, i.e. the v0.1.1 release referenced by the audit finding), not at an earlier tag. The version selector appears exactly once in the URL and both commands inherit it.
R4: No other README content changes: the surrounding prose, command shape (`curl -fsSL <url> | bash`), options and section structure stay as they are, except for the URL itself.

R5: If the chosen URL names a release tag that is not yet published at commit time, the README names the newest published tag instead and the discrepancy is recorded in the task report; README must never advertise a tag that does not resolve.

R6: The existing test suite passes, and tests/test_readme_install.py either already fails on the stale URL (and therefore now passes) or is extended to assert R1 and R2 without weakening any existing assertion.
R7: No change to install.sh, forge_code/*, pyproject.toml or the release directories is introduced by this task.
acceptance: A1: A grep for `v0.1.0/install.sh` in README.md returns nothing.
A2: All install-script URLs found in README.md are identical, and there are at least two of them (one in the install command, one in the uninstall command).
A3: The version selector in the README install-script URL equals the version documented as the current release, and the URL is fetchable (HTTP 200) from the public repository.
A4: The README diff contains only URL changes, reviewable as a small, self-contained change.
A5: `python -m pytest` passes for the whole repository, including tests/test_readme_install.py.
A6: `git diff --name-only` lists only README.md and, optionally, tests/test_readme_install.py.
plan_goal: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH

command: awk '/^### Update$/{f=1;next} /^#/{f=0} f' README.md | grep -Fx -e 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/main/install.sh | sh'
awk '/^### Uninstall$/{f=1;next} /^#/{f=0} f' README.md | grep -Fx -e 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall'
test "$(git show --name-only --format= HEAD | sed '/^$/d' | sort | tr '\n' ' ')" = "README.md tests/test_cli.py tests/test_readme_install.py "

for p in install.sh tests/test_install.py tests/test_check_cleanup.py CHANGELOG.md; do git show --name-only --format= HEAD | grep -qxF "$p" && exit 1; done; for p in install.sh tests/test_install.py tests/test_check_cleanup.py; do test -n "$(git status --porcelain -- "$p")" || exit 1; done; exit 0

result.summary: README.md now documents exactly one install-script URL, the versionless canonical `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/main/install.sh`, in the `## Install` one-liner, the `### Update` block and the `### Uninstall` block; the previous `/v0.1.1/install.sh` paths were replaced and no `/v<tag>/install.sh` path remains. Prose, command shape (`| sh`, `| sh -s -- --uninstall`), options and section structure are unchanged. tests/test_readme_install.py's text-only guard (`assert_single_install_script_url`) rejects a stale `v0.1.0` install-script path, any tag-pinned `/v<tag>/install.sh` path, fewer than two install-script URLs and any URL other than the single canonical string; the rejection cases are proven by assertRaises on the guard itself (stale tag, divergent tag, another branch, missing URL, stale URL anywhere in the document) and the module imports only re, unittest and pathlib, so it needs no network. tests/test_cli.py's ReadmeTest asserts the canonical versionless URL and rejects tag-pinned install paths. Verified with `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (214 tests, OK) and `python -m pytest -q` (214 passed, 137 subtests). The commit could not be executed: this runtime permits only read-only git commands, so `git add --` and `git commit --only --` were rejected; the three changed paths are unstaged and ready for the runtime commit. Worktree files left untouched and uncommitted by this task: install.sh, tests/test_install.py, tests/test_check_cleanup.py (other tasks' work).; the completion step could not decide what to do with every uncommitted file
assumptions: The newer specification (FR-1 to FR-5, A4/A5) mandates a tag-free default-branch URL, so the versionless `main` installer is used instead of a pinned `v0.1.1` tag; this also satisfies R1, R2 and R5 of the task contract because v0.1.1 is not a published tag in this repository (git tag lists no v0.1.1).
CHANGELOG.md is owned by the release train and was left unmodified; the commit message and all artifacts are English with no tool attribution.
install.sh, tests/test_install.py and tests/test_check_cleanup.py are other work in the same worktree and are not part of this change set.

last_failure.message: R10 and the Technical Requirements say 'the commit is performed by the runtime, not by the agent (the agent's git is read-only)' and that only the three named paths are compared, but they never say how the runtime identifies those paths in a worktree that legitimately contains unrelated pre-existing modifications (install.sh, tests/test_install.py, tests/test_check_cleanup.py). The runtime's commit-selection step therefore reports 'the completion step could not decide which uncommitted files belong to the task', the repository stays uncommitted, and the acceptance item 'the task repository is committed' plus AC9 (commit contains exactly README.md, tests/test_readme_install.py, tests/test_cli.py) can never pass. Drop the statement that the agent's git is read-only and the statement that the runtime performs the commit, keep the rule that the whole working tree is never committed, and leave FR-1 to FR-11 and all acceptance checks unchanged so the existing README canonical-URL work remains valid.

spec_issues.requirement: R3: the install-script URL points at the current release with the version selector appearing exactly once in the URL
spec_issues.problem: It contradicts the accepted specification's FR-4, FR-5 and A4/A5, which require that no install-script path is pinned to a tag and that exactly one distinct tag-free URL exists. Both cannot hold at once, and the README also cannot name v0.1.1 because that tag is not published.
spec_issues.proposal: Keep the tag-free canonical default-branch URL as the specification's FR-1 to FR-5 require, and drop R3's version-selector requirement from the task contract.

spec_issues.requirement: R10/R11: the agent stages and commits exactly README.md, tests/test_readme_install.py and tests/test_cli.py and verifies the commit
spec_issues.problem: The runtime in this environment allows only read-only git commands, so `git add --` and `git commit --only --` are rejected and no commit or `git show --name-only --format= HEAD` verification can be produced by the agent.
spec_issues.proposal: Let the runtime perform the commit for the three paths the agent reports, and relax R10/R11 to require reporting the changed paths and test evidence rather than a self-executed commit and hash.
